description: Landscape of established ASCVD/CVD risk calculators, with input variables mapped onto the ASCVD Risk Factor Atlas factor set, coverage metrics, ranking, and evidence-grounded strengths/weaknesses.
ranking_criteria: Primary: number of strongly-evidenced (grade A/B) atlas factors covered; tiebreak: total factors covered, then distinct categories covered.

calculators.name: QRISK3
calculators.population: Adults 25-84 without prior CVD (UK primary care, QResearch)

inputs.label: Townsend deprivation score
inputs.note: area deprivation index -> social-deprivation

inputs.label: SBP variability (std dev)
inputs.note: derived variability metric; not represented as a discrete atlas factor

inputs.label: Treated hypertension
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

inputs.label: Severe mental illness
inputs.note: schizophrenia/bipolar/severe depression; no discrete atlas factor (depression exists but SMI broader)

inputs.label: Atypical antipsychotic use
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

inputs.label: Regular corticosteroid use
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

strengths: Broadest input set of any established score: ethnicity (9 groups), deprivation, and multiple comorbidities
Includes CKD, atrial fibrillation, RA, SLE, migraine, severe mental illness, corticosteroids, antipsychotics, erectile dysfunction
Incorporates SBP variability and family history; derived/validated in millions of UK primary-care patients
Captures type 1 and type 2 diabetes separately
weaknesses: UK primary-care-derived; requires recalibration for other health systems
Several inputs are treatment/medication flags (steroids, antipsychotics, treated HTN) rather than biology
No lipid subfractions beyond TC:HDL ratio, no renal biomarker values, no imaging/CAC
Omits Lp(a), hs-CRP, and other novel biomarkers

references.title: Development and validation of QRISK3 risk prediction algorithms

calculators.name: JBS3
calculators.full_name: Joint British Societies 3 (JBS3) lifetime risk / heart age calculator
calculators.population: Adults without CVD (based on QRISK lifetime + JBS3 model)

inputs.label: Treated hypertension
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

strengths: Communicates lifetime risk and 'heart age' to motivate prevention in younger/low-10-year-risk people
Broad QRISK-derived inputs including ethnicity, deprivation, RA, AF, CKD
Emphasizes cumulative exposure and modifiable-factor manipulation
weaknesses: UK-derived (QRISK lineage); needs recalibration elsewhere
Lifetime projections are more assumption-dependent and less validated than 10-year risk
No lipid subfractions beyond TC/HDL, no renal biomarker values, no imaging/CAC or novel biomarkers

references.title: Joint British Societies' consensus recommendations for the prevention of cardiovascular disease (JBS3)

calculators.name: AHA PREVENT
calculators.full_name: AHA Predicting Risk of CVD EVENTs equations

inputs.label: Antihypertensive treatment
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

inputs.label: Statin use
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

strengths: Sex-specific, race-free (removed race, uses region/SDI instead) reducing race-based miscalibration
Adds kidney (eGFR, optional UACR) and metabolic (optional HbA1c) axes absent from PCE
Predicts total CVD including heart failure, not just ASCVD
Offers 10- and 30-year horizons; derived and validated in large contemporary US cohorts (>6 million)
Better calibrated to modern event rates than PCE (which overestimated)
weaknesses: Omits Lp(a), hs-CRP/inflammatory markers, and family history despite strong evidence
No coronary artery calcium or other subclinical imaging input
Optional UACR/HbA1c/SDI often unavailable in routine primary care, so base model dominates use
Still restricted to a small set of traditional factors; most graded A/B atlas factors are unused

references.title: Development and Validation of the American Heart Association's PREVENT Equations

calculators.name: MESA CHD Risk (with CAC)
calculators.full_name: MESA 10-Year CHD Risk Score with Coronary Artery Calcium
calculators.population: Adults 45-85, 4 race/ethnic groups, no known CVD (MESA)
calculators.outcome_predicted: Coronary heart disease (MI, CHD death, resuscitated arrest, revascularization)

inputs.label: Lipid-lowering medication
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

inputs.label: Antihypertensive medication
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

strengths: Adds coronary artery calcium to traditional factors, substantially improving discrimination and reclassification
Multi-ethnic derivation (White, Black, Hispanic, Chinese); includes family history of MI
Directly quantifies subclinical atherosclerosis rather than inferring it
weaknesses: Requires a CT calcium scan (cost, radiation, access)
Predicts CHD rather than global CVD/stroke in the primary model
No renal, inflammatory, or lipid-subfraction inputs; medication flags used

references.title: 10-Year Coronary Heart Disease Risk Prediction Using Coronary Artery Calcium and Traditional Risk Factors (MESA)

calculators.name: Astro-CHARM
calculators.full_name: Astronaut Cardiovascular Health and Risk Modification CAC calculator
calculators.population: Adults 40-65 without CVD (pooled MESA + Dallas Heart + others)

inputs.label: Treated hypertension
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

strengths: Pooled multi-cohort CAC-based ASCVD calculator; adds family history and CAC to standard factors
Predicts hard ASCVD (CHD + stroke) unlike CHD-only MESA score
Improves reclassification over factor-only models
weaknesses: Requires CT coronary calcium scan
Age range ~40-65; US-derived multi-ethnic pooled cohorts
No renal, inflammatory, or lipid-subfraction inputs

references.title: Astronaut Cardiovascular Health and Risk Modification (Astro-CHARM) Coronary Calcium ASCVD Risk Calculator

calculators.name: SCORE2-Diabetes
calculators.population: Adults 40-69 with type 2 diabetes, no prior CVD

inputs.label: Age at diabetes diagnosis
inputs.note: captured as duration/age-at-onset; maps to diabetes-duration

inputs.label: Region calibration
inputs.note: population/geography calibration term, not an individual factor

strengths: Diabetes-specific European model adding HbA1c, age at diabetes diagnosis, and eGFR to SCORE2
Improves calibration in type 2 diabetes vs generic scores; competing-risk derivation
weaknesses: Restricted to type 2 diabetes population; European-calibrated
Omits albuminuria, Lp(a), inflammation, and imaging despite relevance in diabetes
Does not use BMI/waist or lipid subfractions beyond total/HDL

references.title: SCORE2-Diabetes: 10-year cardiovascular risk estimation in type 2 diabetes in Europe

calculators.name: Reynolds Risk Score
calculators.population: Healthy adults without diabetes (Women's Health Study / men's cohort)
calculators.outcome_predicted: CVD (MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, cardiovascular death)
strengths: First major score to add hs-CRP and family history to standard factors, improving reclassification
Sex-specific; validated in healthy non-diabetic cohorts
weaknesses: Derived largely in healthcare-professional cohorts (Women's Health Study), limiting generalizability
Excludes people with diabetes in original derivation
Small input set; no renal, ethnicity, deprivation, or imaging inputs
Requires hs-CRP which is not universally measured

references.title: Development and validation of improved algorithms for the assessment of global cardiovascular risk in women (Reynolds Risk Score)
C-reactive protein and parental history improve global cardiovascular risk prediction: the Reynolds Risk Score for men

calculators.name: PROCAM
calculators.population: Middle-aged men 35-65 (PROCAM cohort; later female/quick versions)
strengths: Uses full lipid panel including LDL and triglycerides (most scores omit TG)
Includes family history of premature MI; well validated for coronary events
weaknesses: Derived in middle-aged German men; original model not applicable to women or other populations without recalibration
Predicts coronary events only (not stroke/global CVD)
No renal, ethnicity, deprivation, imaging, or inflammatory inputs

references.title: Simple scoring scheme for calculating the risk of acute coronary events (PROCAM)

calculators.name: ASSIGN
calculators.population: Adults 30-74 without CVD (Scottish Heart Health Extended Cohort)

inputs.label: SIMD deprivation score
inputs.note: Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation -> social-deprivation

strengths: First score to formally add social deprivation (SIMD) and family history, targeting health inequalities
Includes rheumatoid arthritis; Scotland-calibrated
weaknesses: Scotland/UK-derived; limited external validation elsewhere
Small traditional-factor set otherwise; no renal, imaging, or inflammatory inputs
Largely superseded by QRISK in UK practice

references.title: Adding social deprivation and family history to cardiovascular risk assessment: the ASSIGN score

calculators.name: China-PAR
calculators.full_name: Prediction for ASCVD Risk in China (China-PAR)
calculators.population: Chinese adults >=35 without ASCVD (pooled Chinese cohorts)
calculators.outcome_predicted: Atherosclerotic CVD (CHD death, nonfatal MI, fatal/nonfatal stroke)

inputs.label: Geographic region (North/South, urban/rural)
inputs.note: population/geography calibration term, not an individual factor

strengths: Calibrated to Chinese cohorts with geographic (North/South, urban/rural) adjustment and waist circumference
Predicts ASCVD (CHD + stroke) with 10-year and lifetime horizons; includes family history
Markedly better calibrated than PCE in Chinese populations
weaknesses: Population-specific to China; not transportable without recalibration
No lipid subfractions beyond TC/HDL, no renal, imaging, or inflammatory inputs
Relies on self-reported family history and regional strata

references.title: Predicting the 10-Year Risks of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease in Chinese Population (China-PAR)

calculators.name: FINRISK
strengths: Finland-calibrated with full traditional factors plus BMI and family history of MI
Well validated in serial Finnish population surveys
weaknesses: Finland-specific; requires recalibration elsewhere
No lipid subfractions beyond TC/HDL, no renal, deprivation, imaging, or inflammatory inputs
Largely a regional/national tool with limited international use

references.title: Forty-year trends in cardiovascular risk factors in Finland
references.note: PMID 25422363 is a FINRISK-cohort risk-factor-trends paper, not the derivation of the FINRISK risk function; the definitive FINRISK function derivation reference is not confirmed in this dataset.

calculators.name: ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations
calculators.full_name: 2013 ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations for ASCVD
calculators.population: Adults 40-79, non-Hispanic White & African-American, no ASCVD
calculators.outcome_predicted: Hard ASCVD (nonfatal MI, CHD death, fatal/nonfatal stroke)

inputs.label: Treatment for hypertension
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

strengths: First guideline-endorsed race- and sex-specific US equations; simple, widely implemented
Predicts hard ASCVD (MI, stroke) with 10-year horizon aligned to statin decisions
weaknesses: Overestimates risk in contemporary and higher-SES cohorts
Uses a binary Black/White race variable now considered scientifically problematic
Only 9 inputs; omits triglycerides, family history, CKD, inflammation, obesity, Lp(a)
Derived from older cohorts; poor transportability outside US non-Hispanic White/Black groups

references.title: 2013 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Assessment of Cardiovascular Risk
A systematic examination of the 2013 ACC/AHA pooled cohort risk assessment tool for ASCVD

calculators.name: WHO CVD risk charts (2019)
calculators.full_name: WHO/ISH 2019 revised cardiovascular disease risk charts (21 regions)

inputs.label: Region calibration
inputs.note: population/geography calibration term, not an individual factor

strengths: Region-specific charts for 21 world regions; laboratory and non-laboratory (BMI-based) versions for low-resource settings
Globally applicable, endorsed for population-level screening
weaknesses: Chart-based with coarse risk categories rather than continuous individualized estimate
Very small input set; non-lab version drops cholesterol entirely
No family history, renal, imaging, or inflammatory inputs; limited discrimination

references.title: World Health Organization cardiovascular disease risk charts: revised models to estimate risk in 21 regions

calculators.name: Framingham (2008 general CVD)
calculators.outcome_predicted: General CVD (CHD, stroke, PAD, heart failure)

inputs.label: Treatment for hypertension
inputs.note: treatment/medication-use variable; not a factor in atlas

strengths: Landmark, extensively validated general-CVD model covering CHD, stroke, PAD and heart failure
Simple office-based inputs; foundation for most later scores
weaknesses: Derived from a predominantly White suburban US cohort (Framingham); overestimates in many modern/European/Asian populations
No race/ethnicity, deprivation, renal, or inflammatory inputs
Dated event rates; largely superseded by PCE/PREVENT in the US

references.title: General cardiovascular risk profile for use in primary care: the Framingham Heart Study
Prediction of coronary heart disease using risk factor categories (Framingham)

calculators.name: SCORE2-OP

inputs.label: Region calibration
inputs.note: population/geography calibration term, not an individual factor

strengths: Extends region-calibrated CVD estimation to adults >=70 where other scores are poorly calibrated
Accounts for competing mortality risk in older persons; adds diabetes as input
weaknesses: Still a small traditional-factor set; no lipfractions beyond total/HDL, no renal/imaging/inflammation
European-derived, needs recalibration elsewhere
Older-age discrimination is inherently modest

references.title: SCORE2-OP risk prediction algorithms: estimating incident CVD in older persons

calculators.name: SCORE2

inputs.label: Non-HDL cholesterol (derived)
inputs.note: derived: total minus HDL, primary predictor in model

inputs.label: Region calibration
inputs.note: population/geography calibration term, not an individual factor

strengths: Region-calibrated for 4 European risk areas; predicts both fatal AND non-fatal CVD (SCORE predecessor was fatal-only)
Derived and validated in very large European datasets with competing-risk methods
Uses non-HDL cholesterol, avoiding a separate triglyceride/LDL requirement
weaknesses: European-derived; requires recalibration outside Europe
Narrow input set (age, sex, smoking, SBP, lipids); no diabetes, renal, family history, or imaging
Age range 40-69 in base model (separate OP model needed for elderly)

references.title: SCORE2 risk prediction algorithms: new models to estimate 10-year risk of CVD in Europe

calculators.name: Globorisk

inputs.label: Country/region calibration
inputs.note: population/geography calibration term, not an individual factor

strengths: Explicitly recalibrated to 182 countries using national risk-factor and mortality data
Designed for global/low-resource use; laboratory and office-based versions
weaknesses: Small traditional-factor set (age, sex, smoking, SBP, TC, glucose)
No HDL, renal, family history, imaging, or inflammatory inputs
Calibration depends on quality of country-level input data

references.title: A novel risk score to predict cardiovascular disease risk in national populations (Globorisk)
